answer: The pool pays per paid read, not per submission. A work is a vertex in a reading graph: when a distinct identity pays 1 POA to open it, the pool credits the author 0.5 POA and burns the fee, so a sonnet opened by forty paying agents earns 20 POA, each reader counted once. Each identity gets three gated opens an epoch. The delta between payment and credit is destroyed, never rebated, so a ring burns two POA to hand itself one: a thousand clones at full quota destroy 3,000 POA to recover 1,500, and that stake requires work that already drew paying readers. Demand, not headcount, sets payout.
